cells.remarks: Purports to record a similar grant by the king, of the dēdāhi-karanika right over the villages of Punganūru, Gandiganpalle, Pappūru and Yaδiki to Mallarasa, son of Obala-Nayaku and grandson of Virarasa of the Kaṇḍinya-gōtra. The grant is said to have been made for the merit of Virupākshēśvara in the presence of Kriņāsaktisvāmi. The villages of Palpudungu in the Tommala-sima and Malyavanam in the Punugupalle are each renamed as 'Prangadhēvarāyapuram,' and an officer was given lands in several places as remuneration.

cells.remarks: Purports to register the conferment of the radarikam right over Dharmavaram, in several shares, to 22 families during the reign of Samprati Tipparāja over Penugonda-namāgāni in Guṭṭi-rājya. Also specifies several individuals as the holders of the various offices in the village, and the extent of the lands allotted to them. Mentions a Dhakka-Ōdeya as having constructed the Dhakkanapalli tank and as having brought the idol of Chennakesavasvāmi from Anegondi and consecrated it in the village.

cells.remarks: Purports to record the permission which the king granted, on the occasion of his visit to Bavalipāḍippaṭṭu, (when he was pleased with the reception accorded to him by the chief and four families from the north), to a certain Oṇḍipuḷi-Nayaka, to found a village in the latter's name and to serve as a palaiyakāran with tax-free land under him. The surplus of revenue after deduct- ing 370 pon for himself as the palaiyakāran and 70 pon as nāḍumāi-māniyam, was directed to be sent to the kachcheri at Madurāpuri.

cells.remarks: Incomplete. Seems to record an order of the king while camping at Mañjâkkandi, remitting the taxes on certain lands in different villages, for worship and offering in the temple of Ṡiva (perumâl) Tiyâgarâya-ṠÂvar at Pannapput-tûr alias Srîvatsa-vardhana. It records that in the 2nd year of âlvar Sundara-Pâṇḍya-valaṉ-âdu, during the service called Sundara-Pâṇḍyan-sandi, instituted in the name of one of the princes and for special worship on the day of Mola in the month of Purattâdi in which he was born.. States that the śrîvaimam was known after the name of Sundara-Pâṇḍya-diyâdaraiyar. The writing seems to be of the 14th century A.D.

cells.place: On a black granite pillar set up near the rāma dhvajastambha.
cells.remarks: Records the genealogy of Nallanāṭka and praises his ancestors. States that Vēsanaṭu, the wife of Nūṇkāya Nallanāṭka and daughter of Annayya, the brother of Vēma, had the temple of the god Rāmanātha plastered and golden pinnacles set up over it. She is also said to have incessantly made very munificent gifts for her husband's merit.

cells.remarks: Registers an agreement made by the śivabrāhmaṇas of Tiru-rōvikkudi in Ga[d]giko[n]da-chōluchaturbvēdimangalam in Kuyukkai-nādu, a sub-division of Rājēndrabhīja-vaļanādu, to provide offerings to the god Tiruvuru-Nambiyar set up in the temple by Kavaṇjān Ādavalan-Bhaskar, a member of the alunganam of the village, for the interest on 30 kaśu received by them from the latter. Records also another agreement made by the same persons in the 27th year (of the same king or predecessor) to provide food at midnight service to the stone image of Kshetrēśvandēva from the interest on 60 kaļam of jaḍuly received by them from Govinda-Kramavitan of Kundur.
